messages:
Maya (AE): Hey team — customer POC hitting intermittent 429s during a bulk embeddings import. ~2% of requests failing, mostly spikes around 10:20–10:30 PT. Can someone triage? Request id samples: req_poc_91, req_poc_92

Omar (SE): Which endpoint and concurrency? embeddings or generation?

Maya (AE): /v1/embeddings. They run 50 workers in parallel, batch size 1 -> tokens ~200 each. Example 429 body from their logs: `{"error":"rate_limit","message":"token budget exceeded"}` and headers included `Retry-After: 60` and `x-rw-quota: 12/12`.

Sasha (eng-oncall): Sounds like a combination of per-route burst limit + tenant token budget. Can you paste the raw response headers and one full request id? Also do they set any per-route routing tags? @Omar FYI.

Maya (AE): Pasting header dump: `x-request-id: req_poc_91`, `retry-after: 60`, `x-rw-tenant-quota: 1200/1200`, `x-rw-route-cap: embeddings=20/s, burst=400`. No custom route tag in their client.

Omar (SE): Two quick mitigations: 1) reduce concurrency to ~15–20 and batch up to 4 per request (embeds batch reduces per-item token overhead). 2) request a temporary quota reservation for the trial (timeboxed). Both are low-effort.

Erin (sales-manager): Customer asked about cost. Temporary bump is fine for 24h trial window — tokens still billable, but we can offer to cap the bump with monitoring. I approve a short reservation.

Sasha (eng-oncall): Diagnostic checklist for us: 1) check tenant token_budget via admin API `GET /admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/quota` 2) look at per-route tokens/sec and burst usage in Console > Usage > Routes 3) correlate request ids to node logs (use `req_poc_91`) 4) verify client retry/backoff respects `Retry-After`. If we need immediate relief, I can apply a 24h reservation: embeddings 40/s burst 800.

Maya (AE): I told customer to throttle to 20 workers and to add exponential backoff reading Retry-After. Asking them to retry and send fresh request ids.

Omar (SE): Small helper for clients: prefer batching call `POST /v1/embeddings` with body `{"inputs":[... up to 16 inputs]}` instead of many single-item calls — massively reduces token accounting overhead and rate consumption. Example curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":["a","b","c","d"]}'```

infra-bot: Note: rate-limiter rule updated by Sasha for tenant poc-42 — embeddings reservation applied (40/s, burst 800) TTL 24h.

Sasha (eng-oncall): After reservation, monitor p95 token/sec and error rate. If 429s continue, capture backend node logs around the request ids and check for KV cache eviction spikes or oversized requests.

Erin (sales-manager): I've looped in finance — they want us to note the temporary bump in the trial contract addendum. Maya, please confirm acceptance with the customer before we charge.

Maya (AE): Customer accepted the plan and retried with concurrency 15. They reported failures dropped to 0.3%. I'll collect more request ids and close after end-of-day. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Omar (SE): Nice. When you have the post-mortem req ids, we can recommend permanent best-practice: batching, backoff, or reserved capacity (Dedicated) for production throughput.

Maya (AE): Will do. Closing loop later today.
